card.name: Hedged statements of unknown evidence
card.fires_on: The word or comma that completes a statement that something is unknown, unproven or not studied, such as "is not known", "is unknown" or "no conclusive evidence". It also fires on "human" or "women" in lines saying effects were not evaluated.

modes.label: Unknown value or duration
modes.description: The word "unknown" or "known" ends a claim that a benefit or duration is not established.
modes.example: The usefulness of hemodialysis in the prevention of NSF is<< unknown>>. 5.3 Hypersensitivity

modes.label: Humans not studied
modes.description: "Human" or "women" ends a statement that effects in people were not evaluated or studied.
modes.example: There are no well controlled studies with haloperidol in pregnant<< women>>.

modes.label: No conclusive evidence
modes.description: A comma after a phrase saying evidence is lacking, before a hedged claim.
modes.example: Although there is no conclusive evidence to support this contention<<,>> it is generally accepted that chest tube drainage

card.writes: It pushes toward words of doubt and reported belief, such as questionable, dubious, unreliable and reportedly.
card.plain: It marks sentences that say something is unknown or not proven.
